scripts.name: Bushes
scripts.source:
-- Bushes hide whoever stands in them. Shared so the server (hidden flags for
-- bots) and your client (see-through canopy, hidden name tags) agree on who
-- is covered. A bush is a model of upright leaf discs in workspace.Map.Bushes.

local Bushes = {}

Bushes.ATTRIBUTE = "InBush" -- set on characters by the server
Bushes.CLOAK_ATTRIBUTE = "CloakedUntil" -- server time the Magic Cloak wears off

local cachedFolder: Instance? = nil
local cached: { BasePart } = {}
local dirty = true

-- Every leaf disc on the current map. Re-collected when the map is rebuilt.
function Bushes.leaves(): { BasePart }
	local map = workspace:FindFirstChild("Map")
	local folder = map and map:FindFirstChild("Bushes")
	if folder ~= cachedFolder then
		cachedFolder = folder
		dirty = true
		if folder then
			folder.DescendantAdded:Connect(function()
				dirty = true
			end)
		end
	end
	if dirty then
		dirty = false
		cached = {}
		if folder then
			for _, part in folder:GetDescendants() do
				if part.Name == "Leaves" and part:IsA("BasePart") then
					table.insert(cached, part)
				end
			end
		end
	end
	return cached
end

-- The bush model covering a position, if any. Leaf discs are upright
-- cylinders, so their diameter is Size.Y.
function Bushes.coverAt(position: Vector3): Model?
	for _, part in Bushes.leaves() do
		local center = part.Position
		local radius = part.Size.Y / 2 - 0.4
		local dx, dz = position.X - center.X, position.Z - center.Z
		if dx * dx + dz * dz <= radius * radius then
			local model = part.Parent
			return if model and model:IsA("Model") then model else nil
		end
	end
	return nil
end

return Bushes

scripts.name: CharacterLook
scripts.source:
-- The top-down person from the original: a rounded body in the shirt color
-- with a dark outline, a round head (hair on top) with a skin-colored face
-- crescent at the front, and a soft shadow. Zombies add two arms reaching
-- forward. Used on live characters (server) and skin previews (client).
-- Front is -Z of the root, like every Roblox character.

local Config = require(script.Parent.Config)
local Parts = require(script.Parent.Parts)
local Skins = require(script.Parent.Skins)

local C = Config.CHARACTER

local CharacterLook = {}

local UP = Parts.UPRIGHT

local function darker(hex: string, amount: number?): Color3
	local c = Color3.fromHex(hex)
	local k = amount or 0.62
	return Color3.new(c.R * k, c.G * k, c.B * k)
end

local function attach(root: BasePart, part: BasePart, offset: CFrame, model: Instance)
	Parts.makeVisual(part)
	part.CFrame = root.CFrame * offset -- also correct inside ViewportFrames, which never solve joints
	part:SetAttribute("LookPart", true)
	part.Parent = model
	local weld = Instance.new("Weld")
	weld.Part0 = root
	weld.Part1 = part
	weld.C0 = offset
	weld.Parent = part
end

local function disc(name: string, diameter: number, height: number, color: string | Color3): Part
	return Parts.make({
		name = name,
		shape = Enum.PartType.Cylinder,
		size = Vector3.new(height, diameter, diameter),
		cframe = CFrame.identity,
		color = color,
		anchored = false,
	})
end

local function block(name: string, size: Vector3, color: string | Color3): Part
	return Parts.make({ name = name, size = size, cframe = CFrame.identity, color = color, anchored = false })
end

local function ball(name: string, diameter: number, color: string): Part
	return Parts.make({
		name = name,
		shape = Enum.PartType.Ball,
		size = Vector3.one * diameter,
		cframe = CFrame.identity,
		color = color,
		anchored = false,
	})
end

-- A flat rounded rectangle (w along X, d along Z) whose top is at `top`.
local function roundedRect(
	model: Model,
	root: BasePart,
	name: string,
	cx: number,
	cz: number,
	w: number,
	d: number,
	r: number,
	top: number,
	thickness: number,
	color: string | Color3
)
	local y = top - thickness / 2
	attach(root, block(name, Vector3.new(w, thickness, d - 2 * r), color), CFrame.new(cx, y, cz), model)
	attach(root, block(name, Vector3.new(w - 2 * r, thickness, d), color), CFrame.new(cx, y, cz), model)
	for _, sx in { -1, 1 } do
		for _, sz in { -1, 1 } do
			local corner = disc(name, r * 2, thickness, color)
			attach(root, corner, CFrame.new(cx + sx * (w / 2 - r), y, cz + sz * (d / 2 - r)) * UP, model)
		end
	end
end

-- Hats sit on the head. `s` is the character scale; the hair's top surface
-- is at y = 0.96 * s above the root center and the head is 1.9 * s wide (the
-- caller passes s already scaled for the real head size).
type HatBuilder = (model: Model, root: BasePart, s: number) -> ()

local HATS: { [string]: HatBuilder } = {
	ChefHat = function(model, root, s)
		attach(root, disc("Hat", 1.75 * s, 0.25 * s, "D8DCE2"), CFrame.new(0, 0.95 * s, 0.05 * s) * UP, model)
		attach(root, disc("Hat", 1.45 * s, 0.5 * s, "FFFFFF"), CFrame.new(0, 1.15 * s, 0.12 * s) * UP, model)
	end,
	Headband = function(model, root, s)
		attach(root, disc("Hat", 2.08 * s, 0.25 * s, "D7263D"), CFrame.new(0, 0.72 * s, 0) * UP, model)
		for side = -1, 1, 2 do
			local tail = block("Hat", Vector3.new(0.22, 0.15, 0.9) * s, "D7263D")
			attach(
				root,
				tail,
				CFrame.new(side * 0.18 * s, 0.75 * s, 1.3 * s) * CFrame.Angles(0, side * 0.35, 0),
				model
			)
		end
	end,
	Stem = function(model, root, s)
		for _, x in { -0.35, 0.35 } do
			attach(
				root,
				block("Hat", Vector3.new(0.12, 0.04, 1.2) * s, "C86412"),
				CFrame.new(x * s, 0.98 * s, 0.08 * s),
				model
			)
		end
		attach(root, disc("Hat", 0.35 * s, 0.4 * s, "3E8E3A"), CFrame.new(0, 1.12 * s, 0.08 * s) * UP, model)
		attach(
			root,
			block("Hat", Vector3.new(0.5, 0.06, 0.28) * s, "4CAF50"),
			CFrame.new(0.3 * s, 1.14 * s, 0.15 * s),
			model
		)
	end,
	Visor = function(model, root, s)
		attach(root, disc("Hat", 1.2 * s, 0.12 * s, "7FC8F8"), CFrame.new(0, 0.98 * s, -0.3 * s) * UP, model)
		attach(root, ball("Hat", 0.32 * s, "9AA3AE"), CFrame.new(0.5 * s, 1.0 * s, 0.45 * s), model)
	end,
	Crown = function(model, root, s)
		attach(root, disc("Hat", 1.3 * s, 0.35 * s, "F5C542"), CFrame.new(0, 1.08 * s, 0.08 * s) * UP, model)
		attach(root, disc("Hat", 1.0 * s, 0.37 * s, "B3242F"), CFrame.new(0, 1.09 * s, 0.08 * s) * UP, model)
		for i = 0, 4 do
			local angle = i / 5 * math.pi * 2
			local point = ball("Hat", 0.3 * s, "F5C542")
			attach(
				root,
				point,
				CFrame.new(math.sin(angle) * 0.62 * s, 1.3 * s, 0.08 * s + math.cos(angle) * 0.62 * s),
				model
			)
		end
	end,
}

-- Costume pieces for the animal and character skins, drawn in real studs at
-- scale `s`. Reference points: head center (0, 0), head radius 1.15 * s,
-- head top at y = 0.97 * s, face front at z = -1.05 * s; body 3.6 x 2.1 * s
-- centered at z = +0.1 * s with its top at y = 0.5 * s.
type Kit = {
	dot: (x: number, z: number, d: number, top: number, color: string | Color3) -> Part,
	bar: (
		x: number,
		z: number,
		w: number,
		d: number,
		top: number,
		color: string | Color3,
		yaw: number?
	) -> Part,
	pill: (x: number, z: number, w: number, d: number, top: number, color: string | Color3) -> (),
	box: (x: number, z: number, w: number, d: number, r: number, top: number, color: string | Color3) -> (),
	ball: (x: number, y: number, z: number, d: number, color: string | Color3) -> Part,
}

local function kit(model: Model, root: BasePart, s: number): Kit
	local k = {} :: Kit
	function k.dot(x, z, d, top, color)
		local part = disc("Costume", d * s, 0.05 * s, color)
		attach(root, part, CFrame.new(x * s, (top - 0.025) * s, z * s) * UP, model)
		return part
	end
	function k.bar(x, z, w, d, top, color, yaw)
		local part = block("Costume", Vector3.new(w, 0.05, d) * s, color)
		attach(root, part, CFrame.new(x * s, (top - 0.025) * s, z * s) * CFrame.Angles(0, yaw or 0, 0), model)
		return part
	end
	function k.pill(x, z, w, d, top, color)
		local r = math.min(w, d) / 2
		roundedRect(
			model,
			root,
			"Costume",
			x * s,
			z * s,
			w * s,
			d * s,
			r * s * 0.999,
			top * s,
			0.05 * s,
			color
		)
	end
	function k.box(x, z, w, d, r, top, color)
		roundedRect(model, root, "Costume", x * s, z * s, w * s, d * s, r * s, top * s, 0.05 * s, color)
	end
	function k.ball(x, y, z, d, color)
		local part = ball("Costume", d * s, if typeof(color) == "string" then color else "FFFFFF")
		if typeof(color) == "Color3" then
			part.Color = color
		end
		attach(root, part, CFrame.new(x * s, y * s, z * s), model)
		return part
	end
	return k
end

type Style = (k: Kit, skin: Skins.Skin) -> ()

local STYLES: { [string]: Style } = {
	-- The first zombie: red blotches on the body and arms (red hands come
	-- from the skin's arm color).
	Alpha = function(k, skin)
		local red = skin.accent or "B8323A"
		local spots: { { number } } =
			{ { -1.0, 0.55, 0.9 }, { 1.05, 0.05, 0.7 }, { 0.3, 0.8, 0.55 }, { -0.35, -0.45, 0.4 } }
		for _, spot in spots do
			k.dot(spot[1], spot[2], spot[3], 0.52, red)
		end
		for side = -1, 1, 2 do
			k.dot(side * 1.35, -0.75, 0.45, 0.7, red)
		end
	end,
	Robot = function(k, skin)
		k.bar(0, -0.6, 1.5, 0.35, 1.02, skin.accent or "00E5FF") -- visor
		for side = -1, 1, 2 do
			k.dot(side * 1.1, 0, 0.35, 0.95, "7F8C8D") -- bolts
		end
		k.bar(0, 0.2, 0.08, 0.8, 1.05, "7F8C8D") -- antenna stalk (seen from above)
		k.ball(0, 1.2, 0.55, 0.38, "E5484D")
	end,
	Pirate = function(k, skin)
		k.dot(0, 0.1, 2.0, 1.15, "1C1C1C") -- tricorn hat
		k.bar(0, -0.75, 1.5, 0.3, 1.16, "1C1C1C")
		k.dot(0, 0.1, 0.35, 1.18, "F4F4F4") -- skull badge
		k.dot(0.35, -0.85, 0.32, 1.05, "1C1C1C") -- eye patch
		k.bar(-0.1, -0.7, 1.4, 0.06, 1.04, "1C1C1C", -0.5)
	end,
	Cowboy = function(k, skin)
		k.dot(0, 0.05, 2.9, 1.1, skin.accent or "8B5A2B") -- wide brim
		k.pill(0, 0.05, 1.4, 1.05, 1.3, "6B4226") -- crown
		k.bar(0, 0.05, 1.42, 0.18, 1.31, "1C1C1C")
	end,
	Alien = function(k, skin)
		for side = -1, 1, 2 do
			k.pill(side * 0.45, -0.55, 0.5, 0.75, 1.02, skin.accent or "1C1C1C") -- big eyes
			k.bar(side * 0.4, 0.35, 0.08, 0.9, 1.05, skin.hair, side * 0.4) -- antennae
			k.ball(side * 0.6, 1.2, 0.75, 0.32, "C6FF00")
		end
	end,
	Knight = function(k, skin)
		k.dot(0, 0, 2.45, 1.05, "BDC3C7") -- helmet
		k.bar(0, -0.75, 1.4, 0.14, 1.07, "2B2B30") -- visor slit
		k.pill(0, 0.5, 0.45, 1.4, 1.12, skin.accent or "C0392B") -- plume
	end,
	-- The awesome face, drawn on top of the head (its forehead toward the
	-- front): yellow with a thick black outline, big white eyes looking up
	-- and a huge open grin with a pink tongue.
	Awesome = function(k, skin)
		local black = "141414"
		k.dot(0, 0, 2.62, 1.0, black)
		k.dot(0, 0, 2.34, 1.02, skin.hair)
		-- The grin: a black-rimmed half-moon, its top half hidden under
		-- yellow so the top edge is nearly flat.
		k.dot(0, 0.12, 1.8, 1.04, black)
		k.dot(0, 0.12, 1.58, 1.06, skin.accent or "7A1F45")
		k.pill(0, 0.6, 0.78, 0.44, 1.08, "F27A9B") -- tongue
		k.pill(0, -0.33, 2.0, 0.76, 1.1, skin.hair)
		k.bar(0, 0.1, 1.74, 0.11, 1.12, black)
		-- Eyes: tall white ovals with the pupils up top.
		for side = -1, 1, 2 do
			k.pill(side * 0.4, -0.45, 0.6, 0.84, 1.14, black)
			k.pill(side * 0.4, -0.45, 0.46, 0.7, 1.16, "FFFFFF")
			k.dot(side * 0.43, -0.62, 0.3, 1.18, black)
		end
	end,
}

-- A zombie's arms reach this far in front of its body center (studs at
-- scale 1), this far either side. Infection and furniture pushing both use
-- this box, in the zombie's own frame.
CharacterLook.ZOMBIE_ARM_REACH = 2.65
CharacterLook.ZOMBIE_ARM_SPAN = 1.85

-- Where the right hand holds an item, relative to the root (front is -Z).
function CharacterLook.grip(scale: number): CFrame
	return CFrame.new(1.2 * scale, 0.6 * scale, -0.95 * scale)
end

-- Builds (or rebuilds) the look on `model`. Keeps an existing part named
-- "Head" so anything attached to it (name tag, chat bubbles) survives.
-- The part named "Head" (name tags hang off it), reused across rebuilds.
local function placeHead(
	model: Model,
	root: BasePart,
	diameter: number,
	thickness: number,
	color: string,
	at: CFrame
)
	local head = model:FindFirstChild("Head") :: Part?
	if head then
		local oldWeld = head:FindFirstChild("Weld")
		if oldWeld then
			oldWeld:Destroy()
		end
	else
		head = Instance.new("Part")
	end
	assert(head, "head")
	head.Name = "Head"
	head.Shape = Enum.PartType.Cylinder
	head.Size = Vector3.new(thickness, diameter, diameter)
	head.Color = Color3.fromHex(color)
	head.Material = Enum.Material.SmoothPlastic
	head.CastShadow = false
	head.TopSurface = Enum.SurfaceType.Smooth
	head.BottomSurface = Enum.SurfaceType.Smooth
	attach(root, head, at * UP, model)
end

local function lighter(hex: string, amount: number): Color3
	local c = Color3.fromHex(hex)
	return Color3.new(c.R + (1 - c.R) * amount, c.G + (1 - c.G) * amount, c.B + (1 - c.B) * amount)
end

-- Animals ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Animal skins get their own body instead of the person shape: long and thin
-- from above with the head in front (-Z), paws, ears and a tail. Sizes are
-- studs at scale 1. Colors: shirt = body, hair = head, skin = muzzle / light
-- parts, accent = ears, paws and other dark parts.

type Animal = {
	body: "Quadruped" | "Bird" | "Fish" | "Frog",
	width: number, -- torso, side to side
	length: number, -- torso, front to back
	head: number, -- head diameter
	snout: { number }?, -- muzzle { width, length } in front of the head
	ears: string?, -- Floppy | Pointy | Tall | Round | Long
	tail: string?, -- Wag | Long | Stub | Cotton | Tuft | Duck
	stripe: boolean?, -- dark line down the back
	whiskers: boolean?,
	patches: boolean?, -- panda markings
	furry: boolean?, -- a fluffy, scalloped edge all round (bears)
	koi: boolean?, -- white and orange patches (the koi)
}

local ANIMALS: { [string]: Animal } = {
	Dog = {
		body = "Quadruped",
		width = 2.3,
		length = 3.1,
		head = 1.9,
		snout = { 0.85, 0.75 },
		ears = "Floppy",
		tail = "Wag",
	},
	Cat = {
		body = "Quadruped",
		width = 1.9,
		length = 2.9,
		head = 1.65,
		snout = { 0.6, 0.4 },
		ears = "Pointy",
		tail = "Long",
		whiskers = true,
	},
	Bunny = {
		body = "Quadruped",
		width = 2.0,
		length = 2.6,
		head = 1.6,
		snout = { 0.5, 0.35 },
		ears = "Tall",
		tail = "Cotton",
	},
	Bear = {
		body = "Quadruped",
		width = 2.8,
		length = 3.5,
		head = 2.0,
		snout = { 1.1, 0.85 },
		ears = "Round",
		tail = "Stub",
		furry = true,
	},
	Panda = {
		body = "Quadruped",
		width = 2.8,
		length = 3.4,
		head = 2.0,
		snout = { 0.85, 0.65 },
		ears = "Round",
		tail = "Stub",
		patches = true,
		furry = true,
	},
	Donkey = {
		body = "Quadruped",
		width = 1.9,
		length = 3.7,
		head = 1.5,
		snout = { 0.95, 1.2 },
		ears = "Long",
		tail = "Tuft",
		stripe = true,
	},
	Frog = { body = "Frog", width = 2.3, length = 2.5, head = 2.0 },
	Penguin = { body = "Bird", width = 2.2, length = 2.8, head = 1.65 },
	Bill = { body = "Bird", width = 2.2, length = 2.8, head = 1.55, tail = "Duck" }, -- the Duck skin
	Shark = { body = "Fish", width = 1.9, length = 4.6, head = 1.9 },
	Koi = { body = "Fish", width = 1.9, length = 4.0, head = 1.8, koi = true },
}

-- Animals are drawn smaller than people (and a bit slimmer still).
local ANIMAL_SCALE = 0.8
local ANIMAL_SLIM = 0.9

local function buildAnimal(model: Model, root: BasePart, scale: number, skin: Skins.Skin, a: Animal)
	local s = scale * ANIMAL_SCALE
	local k = kit(model, root, s)
	local main, head, light = skin.shirt, skin.hair, skin.skin
	local dark = skin.accent or darker(main)
	local edge = darker(main, 0.6)
	local W, L = a.width * ANIMAL_SLIM, a.length
	local headZ = if a.body == "Frog" then -0.85 elseif a.body == "Fish" then -1.35 else -1.45
	local bodyZ = if a.body == "Frog" then 0.4 elseif a.body == "Fish" then 0.5 else 0.45
	local back = bodyZ + L / 2 -- rear end of the torso

	-- An oval (w across, l long) from overlapping discs, rounder toward the ends.
	local function oval(x: number, z: number, w: number, l: number, top: number, color: string | Color3)
		local long, short = math.max(w, l), math.min(w, l)
		local alongZ = l >= w
		local n = math.ceil((long - short) / (short * 0.22))
		for i = 0, n do
			local t = if n == 0 then 0 else -1 + 2 * i / n
			local offset = t * (long - short) / 2
			local d = short * math.sqrt(math.max(0.05, 1 - (t * (long - short) / long) ^ 2))
			k.dot(if alongZ then x else x + offset, if alongZ then z + offset else z, d, top, color)
		end
	end
	-- An oval with a dark outline (and a fluffy, scalloped edge when furry).
	local function outlined(
		x: number,
		z: number,
		w: number,
		l: number,
		top: number,
		color: string | Color3,
		line: Color3,
		furry: boolean?
	)
		if furry then
			local count = math.floor((w + l) * 3.2)
			for i = 1, count do
				local angle = i / count * math.pi * 2
				local px, pz = x + math.cos(angle) * w / 2, z + math.sin(angle) * l / 2
				k.dot(px, pz, 0.62, top - 0.03, line)
				k.dot(px, pz, 0.46, top - 0.01, color)
			end
		else
			oval(x, z, w + 0.2, l + 0.2, top - 0.02, line)
		end
		oval(x, z, w, l, top, color)
	end
	local function eyes(spread: number, z: number, size: number)
		for side = -1, 1, 2 do
			k.dot(side * spread, z, size, 0.97, "1C1C1C")
			k.dot(side * spread - 0.04, z - 0.04, size * 0.35, 0.99, "FFFFFF")
		end
	end

	if a.body == "Quadruped" then
		-- Stubby legs peeking out under the body, paws at the ends.
		local paw = if a.patches then dark else main
		for side = -1, 1, 2 do
			for _, legZ in { bodyZ - L * 0.3, bodyZ + L * 0.3 } do
				outlined(side * (W / 2 - 0.02), legZ, 0.78, 1.0, 0.4, paw, edge)
				k.dot(side * (W / 2 + 0.08), legZ + (if legZ < bodyZ then -0.32 else 0.32), 0.42, 0.42, dark)
			end
		end
		local tail = a.tail
		if tail == "Wag" then
			-- A tail curled up over the rump.
			k.dot(0.3, back + 0.3, 1.05, 0.44, edge)
			k.dot(0.3, back + 0.3, 0.85, 0.46, main)
			k.dot(0.38, back + 0.25, 0.38, 0.47, edge)
			k.dot(0.38, back + 0.25, 0.2, 0.48, main)
		elseif tail == "Long" then
			oval(0, back + 0.85, 0.34, 1.8, 0.42, main)
			oval(0.15, back + 1.6, 0.34, 0.6, 0.43, dark)
		elseif tail == "Stub" then
			outlined(0, back + 0.05, 0.75, 0.7, 0.42, main, edge, a.furry)
		elseif tail == "Tuft" then
			oval(0, back + 0.7, 0.24, 1.5, 0.42, main)
			oval(0, back + 1.4, 0.45, 0.7, 0.43, dark)
		end
		outlined(0, bodyZ, W, L, 0.5, main, edge, a.furry)
		oval(-W * 0.12, bodyZ - L * 0.06, W * 0.4, L * 0.55, 0.51, lighter(main, 0.12)) -- sheen
		if a.stripe then
			oval(0, bodyZ - 0.1, 0.32, L * 0.85, 0.53, dark) -- mane / spine stripe
		end
		if a.patches then
			oval(0, bodyZ - L * 0.2, W * 0.96, 1.05, 0.52, dark) -- panda shoulder band
		end
		if tail == "Cotton" then
			k.dot(0, back - 0.05, 0.9, 0.54, "FFFFFF")
		end
	elseif a.body == "Bird" then
		local beak = skin.accent or "F28C1C"
		for side = -1, 1, 2 do
			oval(side * 0.45, back + 0.2, 0.45, 0.7, 0.36, beak) -- feet
		end
		if a.tail == "Duck" then
			k.bar(0, back + 0.1, 0.75, 0.75, 0.42, main, math.rad(45))
		end
		outlined(0, bodyZ, W, L, 0.5, main, edge)
		for side = -1, 1, 2 do
			oval(side * (W / 2 - 0.12), bodyZ + 0.15, 0.6, L * 0.72, 0.53, darker(main, 0.8)) -- wings
		end
	elseif a.body == "Fish" then
		local fin = skin.accent or darker(main)
		for side = -1, 1, 2 do
			-- A flowing, forked tail and side fins swept back.
			k.bar(side * 0.48, back + 0.55, 0.62, 1.5, 0.42, fin, side * 0.55)
			k.dot(side * 0.85, back + 1.15, 0.62, 0.42, fin)
			k.bar(side * (W / 2 + 0.3), headZ + 1.1, 0.55, 1.3, 0.42, fin, side * 0.8)
		end
		outlined(0, bodyZ - 0.25, W, L + 0.5, 0.5, main, edge)
		oval(0, bodyZ + 0.3, 0.3, 1.5, 0.56, fin) -- dorsal fin
		if a.koi then
			-- White patches and a few dark spots, like a real koi.
			for _, patch in { { -0.3, -0.5, 0.9, 1.1 }, { 0.35, 0.6, 0.8, 1.0 }, { -0.2, 1.4, 0.7, 0.8 } } do
				oval(patch[1], bodyZ + patch[2], patch[3], patch[4], 0.54, light)
			end
			for _, spot in { { 0.4, -0.2 }, { -0.45, 0.9 }, { 0.15, 1.9 } } do
				k.dot(spot[1], bodyZ + spot[2], 0.28, 0.55, "1C1C1C")
			end
		end
		for side = -1, 1, 2 do
			for i = 0, 2 do
				k.bar(side * W * 0.36, headZ + 0.75 + i * 0.2, 0.05, 0.42, 0.57, edge) -- gills
			end
		end
	else -- Frog
		for side = -1, 1, 2 do
			oval(side * 1.2, bodyZ + 0.55, 0.75, 1.7, 0.38, main) -- folded back legs
			k.dot(side * 1.45, bodyZ + 1.45, 0.85, 0.39, dark) -- webbed feet
			oval(side * 1.1, -0.55, 0.45, 0.9, 0.38, main) -- front legs
			k.dot(side * 1.25, -1.0, 0.5, 0.39, dark)
		end
		outlined(0, bodyZ, W, L, 0.5, main, edge)
		for _, spot in { { -0.5, 0.6 }, { 0.55, 0.9 }, { 0.1, 1.25 } } do
			k.dot(spot[1], bodyZ + spot[2] - 0.6, 0.4, 0.52, dark)
		end
	end

	-- Head: round, with an outline; the "Head" part (name tags hang off it)
	-- sits hidden under it. A fish's head is the front of its body.
	local fish = a.body == "Fish"
	local hr = a.head / 2
	if not fish then
		if a.body == "Quadruped" then
			-- Ears go under the head so only their tips show (floppy ones hang
			-- over its sides, so they go on top later).
			for side = -1, 1, 2 do
				if a.ears == "Round" then
					local ex, ez = side * hr * 0.86, headZ + hr * 0.62
					k.dot(ex, ez, 0.92, 0.84, edge)
					k.dot(ex, ez, 0.74, 0.85, dark)
					k.dot(ex, ez, 0.36, 0.86, light)
				elseif a.ears == "Pointy" then
					k.bar(side * hr * 0.72, headZ + hr * 0.45, 0.75, 0.75, 0.84, dark, math.rad(45))
					k.bar(side * hr * 0.72, headZ + hr * 0.45, 0.4, 0.4, 0.85, "FFB3C7", math.rad(45))
				elseif a.ears == "Tall" then
					oval(side * 0.34, headZ + hr + 0.75, 0.55, 2.0, 0.9, head)
					oval(side * 0.34, headZ + hr + 0.8, 0.26, 1.45, 0.91, skin.accent or "FFB3C7")
				elseif a.ears == "Long" then
					-- Donkey ears stick out to the sides, swept a little back.
					k.bar(side * (hr + 0.45), headZ + 0.35, 0.42, 1.35, 0.84, dark, side * math.rad(68))
					k.bar(
						side * (hr + 0.5),
						headZ + 0.37,
						0.18,
						0.95,
						0.85,
						lighter(main, 0.35),
						side * math.rad(68)
					)
				end
			end
		end
		outlined(0, headZ, a.head, a.head * 0.96, 0.88, head, darker(head, 0.6), a.furry)
		placeHead(model, root, a.head * 0.75 * s, 0.3 * s, head, CFrame.new(0, 0.7 * s, headZ * s))
	else
		placeHead(model, root, W * 0.8 * s, 0.3 * s, main, CFrame.new(0, 0.36 * s, headZ * s))
	end

	if a.body == "Quadruped" then
		if a.ears == "Floppy" then
			for side = -1, 1, 2 do
				outlined(side * (hr - 0.1), headZ + 0.2, 0.62, 1.3, 0.94, dark, edge)
			end
		end
		if a.patches then
			for side = -1, 1, 2 do
				oval(side * hr * 0.42, headZ - hr * 0.12, 0.5, 0.65, 0.93, dark) -- eye patches
			end
		end
		local snout = a.snout
		local front = headZ - hr * 0.96
		if snout then
			-- A rounded muzzle poking out past the face, a black nose at its tip.
			local sw, sl = snout[1], snout[2]
			local muzzleZ = front + sl * 0.2
			outlined(0, muzzleZ, sw, sl, 0.95, light, darker(light, 0.7))
			oval(0, muzzleZ - sl / 2 + 0.14, math.min(0.48, sw * 0.6), 0.3, 0.98, "2B2B2B") -- nose
			k.dot(-0.06, muzzleZ - sl / 2 + 0.1, 0.1, 0.99, "FFFFFF")
		end
		if a.whiskers then
			for side = -1, 1, 2 do
				for _, tilt in { -0.15, 0.15 } do
					k.bar(side * 0.5, front + 0.2 + tilt, 0.85, 0.05, 0.99, "1C1C1C", side * tilt)
				end
			end
		end
		eyes(hr * 0.42, headZ - hr * 0.3, 0.22)
	elseif a.body == "Bird" then
		local beak = skin.accent or "F28C1C"
		if a.tail == "Duck" then
			oval(0, headZ - hr - 0.1, 0.95, 0.75, 0.92, beak) -- flat bill
		else
			oval(0, headZ - hr * 0.35, a.head * 0.7, a.head * 0.45, 0.9, light) -- white face
			k.bar(0, headZ - hr - 0.05, 0.42, 0.42, 0.92, beak, math.rad(45)) -- pointy beak
		end
		eyes(hr * 0.4, headZ - hr * 0.3, 0.2)
	elseif fish then
		eyes(W * 0.3, headZ - 0.35, 0.2)
	else -- Frog
		for side = -1, 1, 2 do
			k.dot(side * 0.62, headZ - 0.45, 0.8, 0.93, light) -- bulging eyes
			k.dot(side * 0.62, headZ - 0.55, 0.36, 0.96, "1C1C1C")
		end
		k.bar(0, headZ - 0.85, 1.1, 0.07, 0.92, dark) -- wide mouth
	end
end

function CharacterLook.apply(model: Model, root: BasePart, skinId: string?, team: Skins.Team, scale: number)
	local skin = Skins.resolve(skinId, team)
	local s = scale

	for _, child in model:GetChildren() do
		if child:GetAttribute("LookPart") and child.Name ~= "Head" then
			child:Destroy()
		end
	end

	-- Soft shadow on the floor under the character.
	local shadow = disc("Shadow", 3.1 * s, 0.05, Color3.new(0, 0, 0))
	shadow.Transparency = 0.72
	-- Floor level is HipHeight below the root's bottom (hip height doesn't scale).
	attach(root, shadow, CFrame.new(0, -(C.RootHeight / 2 * s + C.HipHeight) + 0.14, 0) * UP, model)

	local animal = skin.hat and ANIMALS[skin.hat]
	if animal then
		buildAnimal(model, root, s, skin, animal)
		return
	end

	-- Body: outline first (bigger, lower), then the shirt on top.
	local w, d, r, o = C.BodyWidth * s, C.BodyDepth * s, 0.7 * s, 0.14 * s
	roundedRect(
		model,
		root,
		"BodyOutline",
		0,
		0.1 * s,
		w + 2 * o,
		d + 2 * o,
		r + o,
		0.42 * s,
		0.6 * s,
		darker(skin.shirt)
	)
	roundedRect(model, root, "Body", 0, 0.1 * s, w, d, r, 0.5 * s, 0.6 * s, skin.shirt)

	if team == "Zombie" then
		-- Arms reaching straight forward from the shoulders, like the original:
		-- one thick arm in the shirt color with the hand at the end in the
		-- skin color (red claws on the alpha).
		local hands = skin.arms or skin.skin
		local armW, armL, armZ = 0.88 * s, 2.45 * s, -1.35 * s
		local handL = 0.85 * s
		for side = -1, 1, 2 do
			local x = side * 1.36 * s
			roundedRect(
				model,
				root,
				"ArmOutline",
				x,
				armZ,
				armW + 2 * o,
				armL + 2 * o,
				armW / 2 + o,
				0.62 * s,
				0.25 * s,
				darker(skin.shirt)
			)
			roundedRect(
				model,
				root,
				"Arm",
				x,
				armZ,
				armW,
				armL,
				armW / 2 * 0.999,
				0.66 * s,
				0.25 * s,
				skin.shirt
			)
			local handZ = armZ - armL / 2 + handL / 2
			roundedRect(
				model,
				root,
				"Hand",
				x,
				handZ,
				armW,
				handL,
				armW / 2 * 0.999,
				0.67 * s,
				0.05 * s,
				hands
			)
			attach(
				root,
				block("Cuff", Vector3.new(armW, 0.05 * s, 0.08 * s), darker(skin.shirt)),
				CFrame.new(x, 0.655 * s, handZ + handL / 2),
				model
			)
		end
	end

	-- Head: hair-colored disc (kept as "Head"), with the face crescent at the
	-- front made by a skin disc partly covered by a hair disc set back.
	local hd = C.HeadDiameter * s
	placeHead(model, root, hd, 0.3 * s, skin.hair, CFrame.new(0, 0.75 * s, 0))
	attach(
		root,
		disc("HeadOutline", hd + 0.1 * s, 0.3 * s, darker(skin.hair, 0.8)),
		CFrame.new(0, 0.72 * s, 0) * UP,
		model
	)
	-- A little nose poking out past the front of the head, like the original
	-- (not on a face drawn over the whole head).
	local nose = 0.3 * hd
	if skin.hat ~= "Awesome" then
		attach(
			root,
			disc("NoseOutline", nose + 0.1 * s, 0.05 * s, darker(skin.skin, 0.75)),
			CFrame.new(0, 0.89 * s, -0.47 * hd) * UP,
			model
		)
		attach(root, disc("Nose", nose, 0.05 * s, skin.skin), CFrame.new(0, 0.9 * s, -0.47 * hd) * UP, model)
	end
	attach(root, disc("Face", 0.82 * hd, 0.04 * s, skin.skin), CFrame.new(0, 0.92 * s, -0.1 * s) * UP, model)
	attach(root, disc("Hair", 0.74 * hd, 0.04 * s, skin.hair), CFrame.new(0, 0.95 * s, 0.08 * s) * UP, model)

	local style = skin.hat and STYLES[skin.hat]
	if style then
		style(kit(model, root, s), skin)
	end
	local hat = skin.hat and HATS[skin.hat]
	if hat then
		hat(model, root, s * C.HeadDiameter / 1.9) -- hats were sized for a 1.9-stud head
	end
end

-- A standalone, anchored preview model for ViewportFrames.
function CharacterLook.preview(skinId: string, team: Skins.Team): Model
	local model = Instance.new("Model")
	model.Name = "Preview"
	local root = Parts.make({
		name = "HumanoidRootPart",
		size = Vector3.new(C.RootWidth, C.RootHeight, C.RootWidth),
		cframe = CFrame.identity,
		color = "FFFFFF",
		transparency = 1,
		parent = model,
	})
	model.PrimaryPart = root
	CharacterLook.apply(model, root, skinId, team, 1)
	for _, d in model:GetDescendants() do
		if d:IsA("BasePart") then
			d.Anchored = true
			if d.Name == "Shadow" then
				d:Destroy()
			end
		end
	end
	return model
end

return CharacterLook

scripts.name: Config
scripts.source:
--!strict
-- Every tunable number in Brain Tag lives here. Change a value, rebuild, test.
-- Colors are hex strings so this file has no Roblox dependencies (the logic
-- tests in tests/ load it outside Roblox).

local Config = {}

-- Rounds ---------------------------------------------------------------------

Config.MIN_PLAYERS = 2 -- people (or test bots) needed before a round starts
Config.PREP_SECONDS = 60 -- "Outbreak happening in N seconds"
Config.ROUND_SECONDS = 180 -- survival timer after the outbreak (undocumented in the original)
Config.END_SCREEN_SECONDS = 6
Config.ZOMBIE_RATIO = 0.2 -- first zombies = max(1, floor(players * ratio))
Config.FIRST_ZOMBIES_TO_SPAWN = false -- true: send the first zombies to the zombie spawn at outbreak
-- The first zombies are picked this long before the outbreak: their names go
-- red for everyone and they slow down (TURNING_SLOW), then they turn right
-- where they stand.
Config.TURNING_SECONDS = 10
Config.TURNING_SLOW = 0.6
Config.ZOMBIE_RETURN_COOLDOWN = 5 -- seconds between Z presses

-- Maps take turns. Each name is a layout in MapLayout.luau.
Config.MAP_ROTATION = {
	"Neighborhood",
	"Haunted",
	"School",
	"Mansion",
	"PumpkinFarm",
	"DustyGulch",
	"ChristmasTown",
	"SpookyVillage",
	"WitchWoods",
}
Config.ROUNDS_PER_MAP = 2

-- Movement and size ------------------------------------------------------------

Config.BASE_WALKSPEED = 16
Config.ZOMBIE_SPEED_FACTOR = 1.15 -- zombies are faster than humans of the same size
Config.SPEED_MULTIPLIER_CAP = 1.6 -- keeps very high scores from becoming uncatchable

-- 1 + score / 30000, fitted to the two screenshots (500 -> 1.02, 6729 -> 1.22).
function Config.SPEED_MULTIPLIER(score: number): number
	return math.min(Config.SPEED_MULTIPLIER_CAP, 1 + math.max(0, score) / 30000)
end

-- Size also grows with score, much faster than speed: in the original the top
-- player (12,855 points) was about 2.7x the size of a newcomer, and you keep
-- growing after that. Only the collision box stops growing
-- (CHARACTER.MaxRootWidth), so even giants fit through doors.
Config.MAX_SCALE = 8
function Config.SIZE_MULTIPLIER(score: number): number
	return math.min(Config.MAX_SCALE, 1 + math.max(0, score) / 8000)
end

-- Width of the collision box at a size: grows with you up to MaxRootWidth.
function Config.rootWidth(scale: number): number
	return math.min(Config.CHARACTER.RootWidth * scale, Config.CHARACTER.MaxRootWidth)
end

-- How far furniture is kept from your center (the bumper, BumperDiameter at
-- size 1). It follows the collision box, so a giant's bumper never reaches
-- through a wall into the next room.
function Config.bumperRadius(scale: number): number
	local C = Config.CHARACTER
	return Config.rootWidth(scale) / 2 + (C.BumperDiameter - C.RootWidth) / 2 * math.min(scale, 1.5)
end

-- Rewards (score) --------------------------------------------------------------

Config.SURVIVOR_WIN_REWARD = 500
-- Points are saved; when you come back you keep this share of them.
Config.REJOIN_KEEP = 0.9
-- Staying alive pays as you go: every human gets this much every few
-- seconds of the outbreak (a "+10" floats up on their screen).
Config.SURVIVAL_POINTS = 10
Config.SURVIVAL_POINTS_SECONDS = 5
-- Being a zombie costs you: on the same beat, every zombie loses this share
-- of its points (at least ZOMBIE_DECAY_MIN), so they shrink unless they eat.
Config.ZOMBIE_DECAY_FRACTION = 0.02
Config.ZOMBIE_DECAY_MIN = 5
Config.INFECT_REWARD = 50 -- flat bonus for any infection, on top of the points eaten
Config.ZOMBIE_WIN_REWARD = 250
-- Getting eaten costs you this share of your points, and the zombie that
-- ate you gets them (so zombies grow as they feed).
Config.INFECT_STEAL_FRACTION = 0.75 -- getting eaten costs most of your points

-- Immunity (pills) ----------------------------------------------------------------

Config.IMMUNITY_MAX = 100
Config.IMMUNITY_WEIGHT = 0.8 -- pick weight = 1 - immunity/100 * this

-- Camera ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Config.CAMERA_HEIGHT = 175
Config.CAMERA_FOV = 20 -- narrow field of view = near-orthographic flat 2D look
Config.CAMERA_SMOOTHING = 0 -- 0 = locked to you like the original; e.g. 12 for a soft follow
Config.CAMERA_ZOOMS = { Close = 140, Normal = 175, Far = 220 }
Config.CAMERA_GROWTH = 0.35 -- you see this much more around you per extra unit of your size
-- The camera never goes higher than this: beyond it, it widens its view
-- instead. (Roblox only draws lights near the camera: a giant's camera
-- 600 studs up lost its lantern on dark maps.)
Config.CAMERA_MAX_EYE = 260

-- How much more of the world you see at a size (1 at size 1).
function Config.viewGrowth(scale: number): number
	return 1 + (scale - 1) * Config.CAMERA_GROWTH
end

-- Character look (studs, at scale 1) -------------------------------------------------

Config.CHARACTER = {
	-- The collision box is narrower than the drawn body so even the biggest
	-- players (MAX_SCALE) still fit through a 7-stud doorway.
	RootWidth = 2.2,
	MaxRootWidth = 5.5, -- never wider than this, however big you grow (doors are 6+)
	RootHeight = 2,
	HipHeight = 1,
	BodyWidth = 3.6, -- shoulders, side to side
	BodyDepth = 2.1, -- front to back
	HeadDiameter = 2.3,
	-- Characters bump into each other with an invisible cylinder this wide
	-- (only other characters collide with it, so doors still fit).
	ShellDiameter = 3,
	-- Furniture keeps a little space from you: only furniture collides with
	-- this wider invisible cylinder, so you never end up right on top of
	-- what you push.
	BumperDiameter = 4.4,
}

Config.COLORS = {
	SelfName = "9BE22D", -- your own name tag (lime)
	OtherName = "FFFFFF",
	VipName = "F5C542",
	ZombieText = "E0303A",
	Panel = "1E1E1E",
	SystemMessage = "FFD54A",
	Accent = "3B82F6",
	Good = "4CC35A",
}

-- Furniture physics ---------------------------------------------------------------------

-- How hard each weight class is to move. Pushers add their strength (size
-- squared), and a piece moves at walk speed * (1 - mass / strength), capped
-- at PUSH_MAX_FRACTION. At size 1 a couch moves at a third of your speed and a
-- pool table or piano only creeps; at size 2 both move easily. Pushers team
-- up, and a line of people walking into each other's backs adds up too.
Config.FURNITURE_MASS = { Light = 0.15, Medium = 0.45, Heavy = 0.68, Massive = 0.9 }
Config.PUSH_MAX_FRACTION = 0.9
-- Each person behind the one touching a piece lends this share of their
-- (already compounded) strength, so five zombies in a queue shove like ~3.7.
Config.PUSH_CHAIN_SHARE = 0.85
-- Zombies are stronger than humans of the same size: furniture, a weapon held
-- out at them, a barricade standoff.
Config.ZOMBIE_STRENGTH = 1.5
Config.FURNITURE_DENSITY = { Light = 0.4, Medium = 0.9, Heavy = 1.8, Massive = 3 }
Config.FURNITURE_MAX_SPEED = 22
Config.FURNITURE_RELEASE_SECONDS = 0.6 -- your client stops driving a piece this long after you stop pushing
Config.FURNITURE_SPIN = 0.07 -- how much off-center pushes rotate a piece
-- Grabbing, like the original: hold F (L2, or GRAB on a phone) next to a
-- piece and it comes with you, pulled or pushed, keeping its place beside
-- you. Heavy pieces slow you down (a massive one won't come alone). Humans
-- only.
Config.GRAB_REACH = 2.5 -- how far past your bumper a piece can be to grab it
Config.GRAB_BREAK = 4 -- you let go when the piece lags this far behind (stuck on a wall)
Config.GRAB_FOLLOW = 10 -- how hard a held piece catches up to its place
-- A piece starts moving this far (studs, at size 1) before it reaches your
-- bumper, so you push it from a little way off instead of walking into it.
Config.PUSH_REACH = 1.4

-- Bushes ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Walk into a bush to hide: it covers you from above, your name tag
-- disappears for everyone outside it, and bots can't find you unless they
-- come this close.
Config.BUSH_HEIGHT = 9 -- canopy top, taller than the biggest character
Config.BUSH_REVEAL_DISTANCE = 9
Config.BUSH_SEE_THROUGH = 0.55 -- the bush you're in fades this much on your screen

-- Items -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Config.PICKUP_RADIUS = 6
Config.INVENTORY_SLOTS = 3 -- items you can carry; keys 1-3 switch which one is in your hand
Config.GROUND_ITEMS_MIN = 1 -- items are rare: mostly you buy them
Config.GROUND_ITEMS_MAX = 2
Config.RARE_CHANCE = 0.05
Config.KNOCKBACK_SECONDS = 0.3 -- how long a shove lasts (stun is per item)
-- Held melee weapons are solid but not bouncy: someone pressing on the
-- shaft is held off it and pushes the holder back, shared by size squared
-- (times the weapon's firmness). This is how fast an overlap is undone.
Config.SHAFT_SOFTNESS = 12
Config.SHAFT_FURNITURE_FACTOR = 0.8 -- push speed while standing still / turning, as a share of walk speed
-- Soft force fields you feel on your own screen (client ForceField): how
-- fast people / weapons push you apart per stud of overlap, and the caps.
Config.FIELD_BODY = 10
Config.FIELD_BODY_MAX = 14
Config.FIELD_WEAPON = 14
Config.FIELD_WEAPON_MAX = 24
Config.FIELD_RECOIL = 14 -- someone pressing on your weapon pushes you back this hard (by their share)
-- Furniture is solid to weapons: a piece pressed into your weapon (or your
-- weapon pressed into one that can't give) pushes you back this hard per
-- stud, so the weapon bounces off instead of sinking in.
Config.FIELD_FURNITURE = 30

-- Wizard ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Config.WIZARD_SHOP_RADIUS = 10
Config.WIZARD_ARRIVE_MIN = 8 -- seconds into the prep phase
Config.WIZARD_ARRIVE_MAX = 40

-- Admins ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- The admin panel (F2, or the ADMIN button) is open to: everyone while testing
-- in Studio, the experience's owner (or rank 254+ in the owning group), and
-- these UserIds.
Config.ADMIN_USER_IDS = {} :: { number }

-- Saving ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Config.DATASTORE_NAME = "BrainTag_v1"
Config.LEADERBOARD_STORE_NAME = "BrainTag_BestScores_v1" -- best single visit
Config.AUTOSAVE_SECONDS = 90
Config.TOP_SCORES_REFRESH_SECONDS = 120

-- Test bots (Studio only) ---------------------------------------------------------------------

-- Bots join every server, live games included (see BotService for their
-- names and difficulty levels; Mario Robles is the hardest).
Config.BOTS = true
Config.BOTS_MIN = 10 -- each round picks a bot count in this range
Config.BOTS_MAX = 14
Config.MAX_PARTICIPANTS = 40 -- bots make room as real players join
Config.BOTS_WITH_SKINS = 3 -- how many bots wear special skins; the rest look classic
Config.BOT_WEAPON_CHANCE = 0.2 -- chance a bot starts a round with a (cheap) weapon
Config.BOT_MAX_ITEM_PRICE = 1000 -- bots only pick up common items up to this score price

-- Characters bump into each other (human/human, zombie/zombie and
-- zombie/human). Set false to let everyone walk through each other.
Config.PLAYERS_COLLIDE = true

-- Sounds ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Every sound is built from files that ship with Roblox (see the client's
-- SoundBank). To swap one for an audio asset you own, paste its id here by
-- name, e.g. Squeak = "rbxassetid://1234567890". Names: Whoosh, Lunge, Swish,
-- Hit, Clang, Squeak, Boing, Pop, Twang, Gulp, Slip, Shoot, Shotgun, Boom,
-- Splat, Plunge, Freeze, Bubble, WallBreak, Bump, Infect, Groan, Pickup, Drop,
-- Eat, Warp, Outbreak, RoundWin, RoundLose, Tick, TickFinal, UiClick, Buy,
-- Error, Wizard, Spray, Blower, Scrape, Footsteps.

Config.SOUND_OVERRIDES = {} :: { [string]: string }

-- Monetization ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Create these on create.roblox.com > your experience > Monetization, then paste
-- the ids here. A 0 means "not set up yet": the Robux shop hides it in live
-- servers and shows a "set up in Config" card in Studio. Suggested prices are
-- in README.md.

Config.MONETIZATION = {
	GamePasses = {
		VIP = 0, -- gold name, [VIP] chat tag, +20% score, VIP skins
		DoubleScore = 0, -- +100% score from every reward
		StarterKit = 0, -- start every round holding a Bat
		Lucky = 0, -- rare roll chance 5% -> 15%
	},
	Products = {
		InstantBat = 0,
		InstantSpear = 0,
		InstantShotgun = 0,
		InstantAncientSpear = 0, -- the super rare spear: Robux only, the one weapon that strikes
		ImmunityShot = 0, -- +50 immunity right now
		ScoreBoost30 = 0, -- 2x score for 30 minutes (stacks time)
		SkinDuck = 0,
		SkinAstronaut = 0,
		SkinDog = 0,
		SkinPanda = 0,
		SkinRobot = 0,
		SkinAlien = 0,
		SkinShark = 0,
		SkinAwesome = 0,
	},
	VIP_SCORE_BONUS = 0.2,
	DOUBLE_SCORE_BONUS = 1,
	BOOST_SCORE_BONUS = 1,
	SCORE_BOOST_SECONDS = 30 * 60,
	LUCKY_RARE_CHANCE = 0.15,
	IMMUNITY_SHOT_AMOUNT = 50,
}

-- Ids saved in the place itself win over the zeros above: attributes on
-- ReplicatedStorage named "Pass_<key>" or "Product_<key>" (for example
-- Product_InstantBat = 1234567890). Updates to the game's code never touch
-- them. See README "Setting up Robux items".
do
	local function load(storage: Instance, prefix: string, ids: { [string]: number })
		for key in ids do
			local saved = storage:GetAttribute(prefix .. key)
			if typeof(saved) == "number" and saved > 0 then
				ids[key] = saved
			end
		end
	end
	-- Outside Roblox (tests, tools) there is no place to read, so skip quietly.
	pcall(function()
		local storage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
		load(storage, "Pass_", Config.MONETIZATION.GamePasses :: any)
		load(storage, "Product_", Config.MONETIZATION.Products :: any)
	end)
end

return Config

scripts.name: FurniturePush
scripts.source:
-- Shared pushing rules, so your client (for the pieces it drives) and the
-- server (for bots and contested pieces) move furniture identically.
--
-- Each pusher adds a desired velocity weighted by their strength (size
-- squared). A piece moves at the strength-weighted average of those
-- velocities, slowed by its mass: equal pushes from opposite sides cancel,
-- and a big player shoves what a small one can't. With nobody pushing, a
-- piece stops dead: there is no sliding.

local Config = require(script.Parent.Config)
local RoundRules = require(script.Parent.RoundRules)

local FurniturePush = {}

FurniturePush.OWNER_ATTRIBUTE = "OwnerUserId" -- UserId of the client driving a piece (0 = server)

export type Push = { weighted: Vector3, strength: number, torque: number }
export type Pushes = { [BasePart]: Push }

function FurniturePush.weightOf(body: BasePart): string
	local model = body.Parent
	local weight = model and model:GetAttribute("Weight")
	return if typeof(weight) == "string" then weight else "Medium"
end

function FurniturePush.mass(body: BasePart): number
	return (Config.FURNITURE_MASS :: { [string]: number })[FurniturePush.weightOf(body)] or 0.45
end

-- How far furniture is kept from a mover's center (CharacterService's
-- bumper).
function FurniturePush.bumperRadius(scale: number): number
	return Config.bumperRadius(scale)
end

-- Box in front of a mover heading `dir`: from just inside the bumper to
-- PUSH_REACH beyond it, so a piece starts moving before you reach it.
function FurniturePush.moverProbe(root: BasePart, dir: Vector3, scale: number): (CFrame, Vector3)
	local bumper = FurniturePush.bumperRadius(scale)
	local grow = math.min(scale, 1.5) -- like the bumper: never reaching through walls
	local from = bumper - 0.6 * grow
	local to = bumper + Config.PUSH_REACH * grow
	local center = root.Position + dir * ((from + to) / 2)
	local size = Vector3.new(math.max(bumper * 1.6, root.Size.X), root.Size.Y + 1, to - from)
	return CFrame.lookAt(center, center + dir), size
end

-- Box along a held weapon, from the hand to the tip, `guard` studs either
-- side of the shaft (Items: thick bat, thin spear).
function FurniturePush.itemProbe(
	root: BasePart,
	grip: CFrame,
	aim: Vector3,
	reach: number,
	guard: number?
): (CFrame, Vector3)
	local hand = (root.CFrame * grip).Position
	local start = Vector3.new(hand.X, root.Position.Y, hand.Z)
	local center = start + aim * (reach / 2)
	return CFrame.lookAt(center, center + aim), Vector3.new((guard or 0.5) * 2, root.Size.Y + 1, reach)
end

-- Box over a zombie's outstretched arms, from the front of its body to its
-- hands (CharacterLook's arm box). The arms are solid to furniture too.
function FurniturePush.armsProbe(
	root: BasePart,
	scale: number,
	reach: number,
	span: number
): (CFrame, Vector3)
	local look = Vector3.new(root.CFrame.LookVector.X, 0, root.CFrame.LookVector.Z)
	look = if look.Magnitude > 0.01 then look.Unit else Vector3.new(0, 0, -1)
	local from = root.Size.Z / 2 - 0.2
	-- A giant's arms push only just past its bumper, never through a wall.
	local to = math.min(reach * scale, FurniturePush.bumperRadius(scale) + 1.2)
	local center = root.Position + look * ((from + to) / 2)
	return CFrame.lookAt(center, center + look),
		Vector3.new(span * 2 * math.min(scale, 2.5), root.Size.Y + 1, math.max(0.5, to - from))
end

-- Held weapons are solid. While you stand still or turn, a piece the shaft
-- overlaps is pushed out of its way: toward whichever side of the shaft its
-- center is on (so a sweep shoves it along), and a little forward. Returns
-- a flat unit direction.
function FurniturePush.shaftExit(hand: Vector3, aim: Vector3, body: BasePart): Vector3
	local rel = Vector3.new(body.Position.X - hand.X, 0, body.Position.Z - hand.Z)
	local side = rel - aim * rel:Dot(aim)
	if side.Magnitude < 0.3 then
		return aim
	end
	return (side.Unit + aim * 0.5).Unit
end

function FurniturePush.add(pushes: Pushes, body: BasePart, desired: Vector3, strength: number, at: Vector3?)
	local flat = Vector3.new(desired.X, 0, desired.Z)
	local push = pushes[body]
	if not push then
		push = { weighted = Vector3.zero, strength = 0, torque = 0 }
		pushes[body] = push
	end
	assert(push, "push")
	push.weighted += flat * strength
	push.strength += strength
	if at then
		-- Vertical part of (r x v): off-center pushes turn the piece a little.
		local r = at - body.Position
		push.torque += (r.Z * flat.X - r.X * flat.Z) * strength
	end
end

-- The velocity and spin (radians/second about Y) a piece should have.
function FurniturePush.resolve(body: BasePart, push: Push): (Vector3, number)
	if push.strength <= 0 then
		return Vector3.zero, 0
	end
	local fraction = RoundRules.pushFraction(FurniturePush.mass(body), push.strength)
	local velocity = push.weighted / push.strength * fraction
	if velocity.Magnitude > Config.FURNITURE_MAX_SPEED then
		velocity = velocity.Unit * Config.FURNITURE_MAX_SPEED
	end
	local size = math.max(1, body.Size.Magnitude / 4)
	local spin = math.clamp(push.torque / push.strength * Config.FURNITURE_SPIN * fraction / size, -1.5, 1.5)
	return velocity, spin
end

-- How deep the segment a-b (flat; `pad` studs thick: a weapon's shaft, or a
-- body when a == b) sits inside a piece, and the flat unit direction that
-- gets it out the shortest way. Depth 0 and no direction when it's clear.
function FurniturePush.overlapOut(a: Vector3, b: Vector3, pad: number, body: BasePart): (number, Vector3?)
	local cf = body.CFrame
	local right = Vector3.new(cf.RightVector.X, 0, cf.RightVector.Z)
	local look = Vector3.new(cf.LookVector.X, 0, cf.LookVector.Z)
	if right.Magnitude < 0.5 or look.Magnitude < 0.5 then
		return 0, nil
	end
	right, look = right.Unit, look.Unit
	local hx, hz = body.Size.X / 2 + pad, body.Size.Z / 2 + pad
	local samples = if (b - a).Magnitude < 0.05 then 0 else 8
	local best, out = 0, nil
	for i = 0, samples do
		local p = if samples == 0 then a else a + (b - a) * (i / samples)
		local rel = Vector3.new(p.X - cf.Position.X, 0, p.Z - cf.Position.Z)
		local lx, lz = rel:Dot(right), rel:Dot(look)
		local dx, dz = hx - math.abs(lx), hz - math.abs(lz)
		if dx > 0 and dz > 0 then
			local depth = math.min(dx, dz)
			if depth > best then
				best = depth
				out = if dx < dz
					then right * (if lx >= 0 then 1 else -1)
					else look * (if lz >= 0 then 1 else -1)
			end
		end
	end
	return best, out
end

-- A held piece: the velocity that keeps it at its place beside the holder
-- (the holder's root plus the flat offset it was grabbed at), and how far
-- it lags behind that place.
function FurniturePush.holdVelocity(root: BasePart, offset: Vector3, body: BasePart): (Vector3, number)
	local target = Vector3.new(root.Position.X + offset.X, 0, root.Position.Z + offset.Z)
	local lag = target - Vector3.new(body.Position.X, 0, body.Position.Z)
	local v = root.AssemblyLinearVelocity
	return Vector3.new(v.X, 0, v.Z) + lag * Config.GRAB_FOLLOW, lag.Magnitude
end

-- How fast someone dragging a piece can walk, as a share of their speed.
function FurniturePush.dragFactor(body: BasePart, strength: number): number
	return math.clamp(RoundRules.pushFraction(FurniturePush.mass(body), strength) + 0.15, 0.3, 1)
end

-- The piece within grabbing reach of a mover (the one it faces, if several).
function FurniturePush.pickGrab(root: BasePart, scale: number, aim: Vector3, bodies: { BasePart }): BasePart?
	local reach = FurniturePush.bumperRadius(scale) + Config.GRAB_REACH
	local best: BasePart? = nil
	local bestScore = math.huge
	for _, body in bodies do
		local rel = Vector3.new(body.Position.X - root.Position.X, 0, body.Position.Z - root.Position.Z)
		if rel.Magnitude < 0.05 then
			continue
		end
		local dir = rel.Unit
		local gap = rel.Magnitude - FurniturePush.extent(body, dir)
		if gap <= reach then
			local score = gap - dir:Dot(aim) * 1.5
			if score < bestScore then
				best, bestScore = body, score
			end
		end
	end
	return best
end

-- How far an oriented piece reaches from its center along a flat direction.
function FurniturePush.extent(body: BasePart, dir: Vector3): number
	local cf = body.CFrame
	return math.abs(dir:Dot(cf.RightVector)) * body.Size.X / 2
		+ math.abs(dir:Dot(cf.LookVector)) * body.Size.Z / 2
end

return FurniturePush

scripts.name: FurnitureSpecs
scripts.source:
--!strict
-- Footprints (studs) and weight classes for every furniture kind. At rotation
-- 0 a piece is `w` wide along X and `d` deep along Z, with its back toward -Z
-- (top of the screen) and its front facing +Z.

export type Weight = "Light" | "Medium" | "Heavy" | "Massive"

export type Spec = {
	w: number,
	d: number,
	h: number,
	weight: Weight,
	decor: boolean?, -- anchored, walk-over decoration (rugs)
}

local Specs: { [string]: Spec } = {
	Couch = { w = 10, d = 3.6, h = 3, weight = "Heavy" },
	Armchair = { w = 3.8, d = 3.8, h = 3, weight = "Medium" },
	Fridge = { w = 4, d = 4, h = 7, weight = "Heavy" },
	Stove = { w = 4, d = 3.6, h = 3.5, weight = "Medium" },
	Sink = { w = 4, d = 3, h = 3.5, weight = "Medium" },
	Toilet = { w = 2.6, d = 3.4, h = 2.6, weight = "Medium" },
	Bathtub = { w = 9, d = 4.6, h = 2.6, weight = "Heavy" },
	Bed = { w = 7, d = 10, h = 2.6, weight = "Heavy" },
	Table = { w = 8, d = 5, h = 3, weight = "Medium" },
	CoffeeTable = { w = 4, d = 3, h = 2.4, weight = "Medium" },
	Chair = { w = 2.4, d = 2.4, h = 2.6, weight = "Light" },
	Bookshelf = { w = 9, d = 2, h = 7, weight = "Heavy" },
	Box = { w = 2.6, d = 2.6, h = 2.6, weight = "Light" },
	Plant = { w = 2.2, d = 2.2, h = 3, weight = "Light" },
	Picture = { w = 4, d = 3, h = 2.2, weight = "Light" },
	Rug = { w = 12, d = 8, h = 0.06, weight = "Light", decor = true },
	-- Added after looking at the original: more, and heavier, things to move.
	Wardrobe = { w = 6, d = 2.6, h = 8, weight = "Massive" },
	Piano = { w = 8, d = 4.5, h = 4, weight = "Massive" },
	PoolTable = { w = 10, d = 6, h = 3, weight = "Massive" },
	Car = { w = 9, d = 16, h = 4, weight = "Massive" }, -- the garage supercar
	Dresser = { w = 5, d = 2.4, h = 4, weight = "Heavy" },
	Washer = { w = 3, d = 3, h = 3.5, weight = "Heavy" },
	Desk = { w = 6, d = 3, h = 3, weight = "Medium" },
	TVStand = { w = 6, d = 2, h = 2.4, weight = "Medium" },
	Crate = { w = 3.4, d = 3.4, h = 3.4, weight = "Medium" },
	-- Clutter of every size (MapLayout drops these into rooms).
	SmallBox = { w = 1.7, d = 1.7, h = 1.7, weight = "Light" },
	BoxStack = { w = 4.4, d = 2.8, h = 3, weight = "Medium" },
	LongCrate = { w = 7, d = 3, h = 3, weight = "Medium" },
	BigCrate = { w = 5, d = 5, h = 5, weight = "Heavy" },
	BloodBox = { w = 4, d = 4, h = 4, weight = "Medium" }, -- summoned by the Blood Staff
	Barrel = { w = 2.4, d = 2.4, h = 3, weight = "Medium" },
	Bench = { w = 6, d = 2, h = 2.4, weight = "Medium" },
	Lamp = { w = 1.8, d = 1.8, h = 5, weight = "Light" },
	Beanbag = { w = 3.4, d = 3.4, h = 2.4, weight = "Light" },
	TrashCan = { w = 2.2, d = 2.2, h = 3, weight = "Light" },
	Aquarium = { w = 6, d = 2.6, h = 4, weight = "Heavy" },
	Arcade = { w = 3.2, d = 3, h = 6.5, weight = "Heavy" },
	VendingMachine = { w = 4.5, d = 3, h = 7.5, weight = "Massive" },
	Treadmill = { w = 3, d = 7, h = 2.4, weight = "Heavy" },
	-- Haunted house.
	Tombstone = { w = 3.2, d = 1.4, h = 4, weight = "Heavy" },
	Coffin = { w = 3, d = 7, h = 2.2, weight = "Heavy" },
	Candelabra = { w = 1.6, d = 1.6, h = 5, weight = "Light" }, -- gives off light
	Cauldron = { w = 3.6, d = 3.6, h = 2.6, weight = "Medium" },
	Pumpkin = { w = 2.4, d = 2.4, h = 2, weight = "Light" },
	JackOLantern = { w = 2.6, d = 2.6, h = 2.2, weight = "Light" }, -- glows
	HayBale = { w = 5, d = 2.6, h = 2.6, weight = "Medium" },
	Scarecrow = { w = 3.4, d = 1.6, h = 6, weight = "Medium" },
	-- Christmas Town.
	ChristmasTree = { w = 5, d = 5, h = 9, weight = "Medium" },
	Present = { w = 2, d = 2, h = 2, weight = "Light" },
	Snowman = { w = 3.4, d = 3.4, h = 6, weight = "Heavy" },
}

local FurnitureSpecs = { specs = Specs }

-- Everything is drawn this much bigger than the numbers above (footprint
-- only), so pieces read clearly at the game's camera distance.
FurnitureSpecs.SIZE_SCALE = 1.15
-- Pieces that sit tight against walls (and the already-huge car and rugs)
-- keep their size.
local KEEP_SIZE: { [string]: boolean } = {
	Beanbag = true,
	Bed = true,
	Bookshelf = true,
	Car = true,
	Dresser = true,
	Lamp = true,
	Rug = true,
	Sink = true,
	Stove = true,
	TVStand = true,
}
for kind, spec in Specs do
	if not KEEP_SIZE[kind] then
		spec.w *= FurnitureSpecs.SIZE_SCALE
		spec.d *= FurnitureSpecs.SIZE_SCALE
	end
end

function FurnitureSpecs.get(kind: string): Spec
	local spec = Specs[kind]
	assert(spec, "Unknown furniture kind: " .. kind)
	return spec
end

-- Axis-aligned footprint size for a rotation in degrees (multiples of 90).
function FurnitureSpecs.footprint(kind: string, rot: number): (number, number)
	local spec = FurnitureSpecs.get(kind)
	local quarter = math.floor((rot % 360) / 90 + 0.5) % 2
	if quarter == 1 then
		return spec.d, spec.w
	end
	return spec.w, spec.d
end

return FurnitureSpecs

scripts.name: ItemModels
scripts.source:
-- Builds the 3D look of every item from simple parts. The grip (where the
-- fist holds it) is the origin and items point forward along -Z.

local Parts = require(script.Parent.Parts)

local ItemModels = {}

type PieceSpec = {
	size: Vector3,
	at: CFrame,
	color: string,
	shape: Enum.PartType?,
	material: Enum.Material?,
	transparency: number?,
}

local Z = Parts.ALONG_Z

local function blockAt(size: Vector3, x: number, y: number, z: number, color: string, rot: CFrame?): PieceSpec
	return { size = size, at = CFrame.new(x, y, z) * (rot or CFrame.identity), color = color }
end

-- Cylinder lying along Z.
local function rod(
	length: number,
	diameter: number,
	z: number,
	color: string,
	x: number?,
	y: number?
): PieceSpec
	return {
		size = Vector3.new(length, diameter, diameter),
		at = CFrame.new(x or 0, y or 0, z) * Z,
		color = color,
		shape = Enum.PartType.Cylinder,
	}
end

local function ballAt(
	diameter: number,
	x: number,
	y: number,
	z: number,
	color: string,
	material: Enum.Material?
): PieceSpec
	return {
		size = Vector3.one * diameter,
		at = CFrame.new(x, y, z),
		color = color,
		shape = Enum.PartType.Ball,
		material = material,
	}
end

local DIAMOND = CFrame.Angles(0, math.rad(45), 0)

-- Flat disc lying face-up (reads as a circle from the top-down camera).
local function discAt(
	diameter: number,
	height: number,
	x: number,
	y: number,
	z: number,
	color: string
): PieceSpec
	return {
		size = Vector3.new(height, diameter, diameter),
		at = CFrame.new(x, y, z) * Parts.UPRIGHT,
		color = color,
		shape = Enum.PartType.Cylinder,
	}
end

-- Cylinder lying along X (sideways across the item).
local function crossRod(length: number, diameter: number, x: number, z: number, color: string): PieceSpec
	return {
		size = Vector3.new(length, diameter, diameter),
		at = CFrame.new(x, 0, z),
		color = color,
		shape = Enum.PartType.Cylinder,
	}
end

local function see(spec: PieceSpec, transparency: number): PieceSpec
	spec.transparency = transparency
	return spec
end

local function glow(spec: PieceSpec): PieceSpec
	spec.material = Enum.Material.Neon
	return spec
end

local function yaw(radians: number): CFrame
	return CFrame.Angles(0, radians, 0)
end

-- The swordfish, drawn flat on its side like the original's sprite: blue
-- back, white belly, a spiky sail fin, a forked tail and a long thin bill,
-- all with a dark outline. Held by the tail, nose forward.
local function swordfish(): { PieceSpec }
	local out: { PieceSpec } = {}
	local LINE, BLUE, BELLY, BILL = "14284A", "2F63B8", "EEF2F7", "D5DCE6"
	local function bar(length: number, width: number, x: number, z: number, angle: number, color: string)
		table.insert(
			out,
			blockAt(Vector3.new(length + 0.18, 0.1, width + 0.18), x, -0.06, z, LINE, yaw(angle))
		)
		table.insert(out, blockAt(Vector3.new(length, 0.12, width), x, 0, z, color, yaw(angle)))
	end
	-- A fin growing out of the body at (x, z), swept back toward the tail.
	local function fin(length: number, width: number, x: number, z: number, out_: number)
		local dir = Vector3.new(math.cos(0.6) * out_, 0, math.sin(0.6))
		bar(length, width, x + dir.X * length / 2, z + dir.Z * length / 2, -0.6 * out_, BLUE)
	end
	-- Forked tail and the thin stalk you hold it by.
	bar(1.4, 0.32, 0.56, 0.47, -0.65, BLUE)
	bar(1.4, 0.32, -0.56, 0.47, 0.65, BLUE)
	-- Body: a spindle of discs, blue on the back (+X) and white on the belly.
	local body = {
		{ 0.05, 0.36 },
		{ -0.4, 0.42 },
		{ -0.9, 0.55 },
		{ -1.35, 0.85 },
		{ -1.85, 1.15 },
		{ -2.4, 1.4 },
		{ -3.0, 1.5 },
		{ -3.6, 1.45 },
		{ -4.15, 1.25 },
		{ -4.6, 0.95 },
		{ -4.95, 0.62 },
	}
	-- Twice as many discs as listed (halfway ones in between) for a smooth edge.
	local smooth = {}
	for i, seg in body do
		table.insert(smooth, seg)
		local nextSeg = body[i + 1]
		if nextSeg then
			table.insert(smooth, { (seg[1] + nextSeg[1]) / 2, (seg[2] + nextSeg[2]) / 2 })
		end
	end
	for _, seg in smooth do
		table.insert(out, discAt(seg[2] + 0.18, 0.1, 0, -0.06, seg[1], LINE))
	end
	for _, seg in smooth do
		table.insert(out, discAt(seg[2], 0.12, 0, 0, seg[1], BLUE))
	end
	for _, seg in smooth do
		table.insert(out, discAt(seg[2] * 0.56, 0.12, -seg[2] * 0.22, 0.03, seg[1], BELLY))
	end
	-- Spiky sail fin on the back, fins underneath, little finlets by the tail.
	fin(1.5, 0.3, 0.62, -3.6, 1)
	fin(1.15, 0.28, 0.66, -3.05, 1)
	fin(0.8, 0.26, 0.6, -2.55, 1)
	fin(0.5, 0.24, 0.5, -2.1, 1)
	fin(1.0, 0.3, -0.6, -3.7, -1)

-- Returns a Model whose PrimaryPart "Handle" (an invisible grip at the
-- origin) has every visible part welded to it. Parts are anchored; callers
-- unanchor them when the item goes into a hand.
-- `scale` (default 1) draws it bigger, for a big holder (Items.reachScale).
function ItemModels.build(itemId: string, scale: number?): Model
	local model = Instance.new("Model")
	model.Name = itemId
	local handle = Parts.make({
		name = "Handle",
		size = Vector3.new(0.2, 0.2, 0.2),
		cframe = CFrame.identity,
		color = "FFFFFF",
		transparency = 1,
		canCollide = false,
		canQuery = false,
		parent = model,
	})
	model.PrimaryPart = handle
	local s = scale or 1
	for i, spec in DESIGNS[itemId] or DESIGNS.Stick do
		local at = spec.at
		local part = Parts.make({
			name = "Piece" .. i,
			size = spec.size * s,
			cframe = if s == 1 then at else at - at.Position + at.Position * s,
			color = spec.color,
			shape = spec.shape,
			material = spec.material,
			transparency = spec.transparency,
			canCollide = false,
			canQuery = false,
			parent = model,
		})
		Parts.weldInPlace(handle, part)
	end
	return model
end

-- Bounding size of an item, for framing previews.
function ItemModels.extents(model: Model): Vector3
	local _, size = model:GetBoundingBox()
	return size
end

return ItemModels

--!strict
-- Item definitions. Prices are in score. Weapons never kill: they shove
-- (knockback, studs per second at the start of the shove) and briefly stun.

export type ItemKind =
	"Melee" -- click to swing
	| "Projectile" -- click to fire one shot
	| "Blast" -- click for a cone blast
	| "Stream" -- hold to spray (water gun, leaf blower)
	| "Trap" -- click to drop a trap at your feet
	| "Consumable" -- click to use up (or use again later, if reusable)
	| "Passive" -- just hold it
	| "Summon" -- click to summon a piece of furniture in front of you

export type Item = {
	id: string,
	name: string,
	kind: ItemKind,
	description: string,
	price: number?, -- sold in the main shop (B) for this much score
	wizardPrice: number?, -- sold by the wizard for this much score
	robuxProduct: string?, -- Config.MONETIZATION.Products key that grants it
	rare: string?, -- id rolled instead on purchase (Config.RARE_CHANCE)
	isRare: boolean?,
	groundWeight: number?, -- relative chance to be scattered on the map
	reach: number?,
	arc: number?, -- degrees
	knockback: number?,
	stun: number?,
	cooldown: number?,
	straight: boolean?, -- shove along the aim line instead of away from you
	firmness: number?, -- held melee: how hard the shaft holds things back (1 = normal, low = it gives)
	hits: boolean?, -- melee: a click swings and knocks zombies back (most only keep them away)
	guard: number?, -- held melee: studs around the shaft it keeps clear
	breaksWalls: boolean?,
	projectileSpeed: number?,
	projectileRange: number?,
	projectileRadius: number?,
	immunity: number?,
	rewardBonus: number?,
	-- Fun extras (see ItemService and the client's Effects):
	sound: string?, -- sound style played on use
	fx: string?, -- little visual on hit or use
	effect: string?, -- "Freeze" | "Bubble" | "Explode" | "Plunge" | "Slip" | "Cloak"
	projectile: string?, -- projectile look: "Potato" | "Pebble" | "Snowball" | "Bubble" | "Duck"
	slowFactor: number?, -- Freeze: speed multiplier while frozen
	effectSeconds: number?, -- how long Freeze/Bubble/Plunge lasts
	radius: number?, -- Explode: blast radius
	tick: number?, -- Stream: seconds between pushes while held
	charges: number?, -- Trap: how many you can drop
	speedBoost: number?, -- Consumable: speed multiplier
	boostSeconds: number?,
	reusable: boolean?, -- Consumable: stays in your hand (use again after the cooldown)
	summon: string?, -- Summon: the furniture kind it brings
	-- (Projectiles with `charges` are used up after that many shots.)
}

	Items[item.id] = item

-- Display order in the shops.
-- How each held melee weapon holds zombies and furniture back (ItemService's
-- shaftStep and FurniturePush): { firmness, guard }. The bat is short but
-- stiff and thick; the pool noodle is long, fat and soft, so zombies squeeze
-- past it; spears and the katana are thin.
local SOLIDITY: { [string]: { number } } = {
	Stick = { 0.8, 0.45 },
	Bat = { 1.7, 0.9 },
	Swordfish = { 1.0, 0.6 },
	Spear = { 1.1, 0.35 },
	AncientSpear = { 1.3, 0.4 },
	RubberChicken = { 0.45, 0.6 },
	PoolNoodle = { 0.35, 0.9 },
	Baguette = { 0.7, 0.5 },
	FryingPan = { 1.5, 1.0 },
	GoldenPan = { 1.8, 1.1 },
	Crowbar = { 1.4, 0.4 },
	Plunger = { 0.9, 0.6 },
	Lollipop = { 1.2, 1.0 },
	Katana = { 1.0, 0.35 },
	InflatableHammer = { 0.5, 1.3 },
	Slap = { 1.0, 0.8 },
}
-- Melee weapons only keep people away while you hold them out. The
-- exceptions strike: the super rare, Robux-only Ancient Spear, and the SLAP.
local HITTERS = { "AncientSpear", "Slap" } -- the SLAP is all about the hit
for _, id in HITTERS do
	local item = Items[id]
	if item then
		item.hits = true
	end
end

for id, values in SOLIDITY do
	local item = Items[id]
	if item then
		item.firmness, item.guard = values[1], values[2]
	end
end

local SHOP_ORDER = {
	"Stick",
	"Pill",
	"RubberChicken",
	"EnergyDrink",
	"PoolNoodle",
	"BananaPeel",
	"Bat",
	"Slingshot",
	"Baguette",
	"Drumstick",
	"FryingPan",
	"WaterGun",
	"PotatoGun",
	"Crowbar",
	"Plunger",

	"Swordfish",

	"Spear",

	"DuckLauncher",

	"Dynamite",
	"Slap",
	"Glock",
	"Crossbow",
	"FartGun",
	"FreezeGun",
	"StackedDynamite",
	"BloodStaff",
	"MagicCloak",
	"Broom",
	"Shotgun",
}
local WIZARD_ORDER = { "GoldenDrumstick", "RarePotatoGun", "GoldenPan", "InflatableHammer" }

local module = {
	all = Items,
	shopOrder = SHOP_ORDER,
	wizardOrder = WIZARD_ORDER,
}

function module.get(id: string?): Item?
	if id == nil then
		return nil
	end
	return Items[id]
end

-- How much longer (and bigger) a held item gets as its holder grows: the
-- drawn model and its reach both use this. Capped so a giant's spear stays
-- a spear.
function module.reachScale(scale: number): number
	return math.max(1, math.min(scale, 3) * 0.9)
end

-- Items that can be scattered on the ground, as { id, weight } pairs.
function module.groundTable(): { { id: string, weight: number } }
	local list = {}
	for id, item in Items do
		if item.groundWeight and item.groundWeight > 0 then
			table.insert(list, { id = id, weight = item.groundWeight })
		end
	end
	table.sort(list, function(a, b)
		return a.id < b.id
	end)
	return list
end

return module

scripts.name: Knockback
scripts.source:
-- A short horizontal shove. Runs on whichever machine simulates the character:
-- the owning client for players (the server asks it to via a remote) and the
-- server for test bots. A LinearVelocity is used because a Humanoid instantly
-- cancels velocity that is simply assigned to its root.

local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")

local Knockback = {}

function Knockback.apply(character: Model, velocity: Vector3, seconds: number)
	local root = character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart") :: BasePart?
	if not root then
		return
	end
	local flat = Vector3.new(velocity.X, 0, velocity.Z)
	if flat.Magnitude < 0.01 or seconds <= 0 then
		return
	end

	local old = root:FindFirstChild("KnockbackForce")
	if old then
		old:Destroy()
	end
	local attachment = root:FindFirstChild("KnockbackAttachment") :: Attachment?
	if not attachment then
		local created = Instance.new("Attachment")
		created.Name = "KnockbackAttachment"
		created.Parent = root
		attachment = created
	end

	local force = Instance.new("LinearVelocity")
	force.Name = "KnockbackForce"
	force.Attachment0 = attachment
	force.RelativeTo = Enum.ActuatorRelativeTo.World
	force.VelocityConstraintMode = Enum.VelocityConstraintMode.Plane
	force.PrimaryTangentAxis = Vector3.xAxis
	force.SecondaryTangentAxis = Vector3.zAxis
	force.ForceLimitMode = Enum.ForceLimitMode.Magnitude
	force.MaxForce = math.max(root.AssemblyMass, 1) * 4000
	force.PlaneVelocity = Vector2.new(flat.X, flat.Z)
	force.Parent = root

	local started = os.clock()
	local connection: RBXScriptConnection
	connection = RunService.Heartbeat:Connect(function()
		local t = (os.clock() - started) / seconds
		if t >= 1 or force.Parent == nil then
			connection:Disconnect()
			force:Destroy()
			return
		end
		local k = 1 - t
		force.PlaneVelocity = Vector2.new(flat.X * k, flat.Z * k)
	end)
end

return Knockback

scripts.source:
--!strict
-- Every map as plain data, in studs. X grows to the right and Z grows DOWN
-- the screen (the camera looks straight down with -Z as "up"). MapBuilder
-- turns a layout into Parts; tests/ checks every layout and tools/ draws them.
--
-- Neighborhood: a road across the middle bulging around a small island
-- house, with a large house above and the same plan turned 180 degrees below.
-- Mansion: one big house modeled on the original's (orange brick rooms,
-- a concrete garage), a pool and an orange shed out back, the road in front.
-- Christmas Town: Santa's workshop, four cottages and a gingerbread house
-- around a town square with a giant tree, under snow.
-- Haunted: night. A big manor of hallways, rooms, closets and secret nooks
-- behind fake walls, outhouses, a crypt, a shed, a graveyard and a pumpkin
-- patch. Every room has a pitch black roof (you see inside only once you're
-- in). These two are generated by tools/map_plans.py.
-- Every built-in map then gets extra clutter (crates and boxes of all sizes,
-- a big piece in bigger rooms) dropped into its rooms; see `clutter`.

local Config = require(script.Parent.Config)
local FurnitureSpecs = require(script.Parent.FurnitureSpecs)

export type Rect = { x1: number, z1: number, x2: number, z2: number }
export type Range = { number }
export type Point = { x: number, z: number }

export type Wall = {
	x1: number,
	z1: number,
	x2: number,
	z2: number,
	horizontal: boolean,
	gaps: { Range }, -- doorway openings along the wall axis
	windows: { Range },
	secrets: { Range }, -- fake wall: looks solid, but you walk straight through
	house: string,
}

export type WallPiece = {
	rect: Rect, -- full footprint including thickness
	window: boolean,
	secret: boolean,
	house: string,
	horizontal: boolean,
}

export type Room = { name: string, floor: string, rect: Rect, house: string }
export type FurnitureSpot = { kind: string, x: number, z: number, rot: number, house: string }
export type House = {
	id: string,
	rect: Rect,
	outline: string,
	size: string,
	wall: string?, -- hex color for its walls (a corn maze); the theme's Wall color if nil
}
export type Bush = { x: number, z: number, r: number, color: string }
export type Door = {
	x: number,
	z: number,
	horizontal: boolean,
	width: number,
	house: string,
	exterior: boolean,
}
export type Island = { walk: Rect, grass: Rect }

export type Layout = {
	name: string,
	title: string,
	bounds: Rect,
	houses: { House },
	walls: { Wall },
	rooms: { Room },
	furniture: { FurnitureSpot },
	itemSpots: { Point },

	islands: { Island },

	patios: { Rect },

	bushes: { Bush },
	humanSpawns: { Point },

	theme: string, -- MapThemes name: colors and lighting
	roofs: boolean, -- every room has a roof hiding it, except the one you're in

local MapLayout = {}

MapLayout.WALL_THICKNESS = 3
MapLayout.WALL_HEIGHT = 12
MapLayout.MAX_WALL_PIECE = 8 -- breakable segment length

type Plan = {
	w: number,

	x1: number,
	z1: number,
	x2: number,
	z2: number,
	gaps: { Range }?,
	windows: { Range }?,
	secrets: { Range }?

	return {

		windows = windows or {},
		secrets = secrets or {},

local function piece(kind: string, x: number, z: number, rot: number?): PlanPiece
	return { kind = kind, x = x, z = z, rot = rot or 0 }

	return { x1 = math.min(x1, x2), z1 = math.min(z1, z2), x2 = math.max(x1, x2), z2 = math.max(z1, z2) }

-- Assembly -------------------------------------------------------------------------------

local function newLayout(name: string, title: string): Layout
	return {
		name = name,
		title = title,
		bounds = rect(-210, -200, 210, 200),
		houses = {},
		walls = {},
		rooms = {},
		furniture = {},
		itemSpots = {},
		road = { sidewalks = {}, asphalt = {}, centerLines = {}, edgeLines = {} },
		islands = {},
		paths = {},
		patios = {},
		pools = {},
		bushes = {},
		humanSpawns = {},
		zombieSpawns = {},
		wizardSpots = {},
		start = { x = 0, z = 0 },
		theme = "Classic",
		roofs = false,
	}
end

local function addHouse(
	layout: Layout,
	id: string,
	plan: Plan,
	ox: number,
	oz: number,
	rotated: boolean,
	outline: string,
	size: string,
	wall: string?
)
	local function px(x: number): number
		return ox + (if rotated then plan.w - x else x)
	end
	local function pz(z: number): number
		return oz + (if rotated then plan.d - z else z)
	end
	local function mapRanges(ranges: { Range }, f: (number) -> number): { Range }
		local out = {}
		for _, r in ranges do
			local a, b = f(r[1]), f(r[2])
			table.insert(out, { math.min(a, b), math.max(a, b) })
		end
		table.sort(out, function(a, b)
			return a[1] < b[1]
		end)
		return out
	end

	table.insert(layout.houses, {
		id = id,
		rect = rect(px(0), pz(0), px(plan.w), pz(plan.d)),
		outline = outline,
		size = size,
		wall = wall,
	})

	for _, w in plan.walls do
		local horizontal = w.z1 == w.z2
		local f = if horizontal then px else pz
		table.insert(layout.walls, {
			x1 = math.min(px(w.x1), px(w.x2)),
			z1 = math.min(pz(w.z1), pz(w.z2)),
			x2 = math.max(px(w.x1), px(w.x2)),
			z2 = math.max(pz(w.z1), pz(w.z2)),
			horizontal = horizontal,
			gaps = mapRanges(w.gaps, f),
			windows = mapRanges(w.windows, f),
			secrets = mapRanges(w.secrets, f),
			house = id,
		})
	end

	for _, r in plan.rooms do
		table.insert(layout.rooms, {
			name = r.name,
			floor = r.floor,
			rect = rect(px(r.x1), pz(r.z1), px(r.x2), pz(r.z2)),
			house = id,
		})
	end

	for _, p in plan.furniture do
		local rot = if rotated then (p.rot + 180) % 360 else p.rot
		table.insert(layout.furniture, { kind = p.kind, x = px(p.x), z = pz(p.z), rot = rot, house = id })
	end

	for _, spot in plan.items do
		table.insert(layout.itemSpots, pt(px(spot.x), pz(spot.z)))
	end
end

-- Point reflection through the map center, used to mirror yards.
local function mirrorRects(list: { Rect }): { Rect }
	local out = table.clone(list)
	for _, r in list do
		table.insert(out, rect(-r.x2, -r.z2, -r.x1, -r.z1))
	end
	return out
end

local function mirrorPoints(list: { Point }): { Point }
	local out = table.clone(list)
	for _, p in list do
		table.insert(out, pt(-p.x, -p.z))
	end
	return out
end

local function bush(x: number, z: number, r: number, color: string): Bush
	return { x = x, z = z, r = r, color = color }
end

-- Neighborhood ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

local function buildNeighborhood(): Layout
	local layout = newLayout("Neighborhood", "The Neighborhood")
	layout.bounds = rect(-150, -182, 150, 182) -- brick wall just outside this
	local B = layout.bounds
	addHouse(layout, "North", LARGE, -110, -150, false, "Blue", "Large")
	addHouse(layout, "South", LARGE, -30, 66, true, "Orange", "Large")
	addHouse(layout, "Island", SMALL, -20, -14, false, "Blue", "Small")

	layout.road = {
		sidewalks = { rect(B.x1, -20, B.x2, 20), rect(-52, -46, 52, 46) },
		asphalt = { rect(B.x1, -14, B.x2, 14), rect(-46, -40, 46, 40) },
